Maladaptive Strategies.value: I detach myself from the memories
become overly compliant when feeling threatened
try hard not think about the trauma

Memory.value: The memory feels like it is happening right now rather than something that is over
When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish
When I remember the event I feel intense rage

Negative Appraisals.value: You can never know who will harm you
I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened
The event happened because of the way I acted

issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: For a male torture survivor, sexual-trauma-specific verbal cues are possible only if sexual torture or sexual humiliation is part of the trauma, but the rest of the profile provides no corresponding sexual content in memory, appraisals, threat, or coping. As selected, this trigger appears disconnected from the trauma representation and is hard to justify clinically.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Exposed to Others: I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me
issues.explanation: The appraisal that others can visibly see what happened to him implies shame/marked visible contamination or exposure. That could occur after torture, but here it is not supported by the memory items, trigger content, or other appraisals, making it feel mismatched with the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Gambling: I gamble to distract myself or feel excitement
issues.explanation: Gambling as a coping strategy is not impossible, but in this profile it is poorly linked to the active formulation. The main connected pattern is triggers ↔ negative appraisals with memory-linked re-experiencing and threat-driven compliance/detachment. Gambling introduces a separate excitement-seeking coping style that is not reflected elsewhere and feels clinically disconnected rather than integrated.

vignette: Seventy-year-old Carlos Hernandez had always been a proud man. As a welder, he took satisfaction in his work, knowing that the bridges and buildings he helped construct would stand for generations to come. But it was not the physical labor or the pride of creation that defined him; it was the unyielding will to survive, forged in the depths of pain and humiliation during his time as a political prisoner under a ruthless regime. The memories of those days still lingered, refusing to be buried beneath the years of freedom. The sound of gunfire, once a signal for chaos, now triggered an avalanche of emotions that Carlos struggled to contain. He remembered the feeling of entrapment, being locked in a small cell with no escape, at the mercy of his captors. Even decades later, the recollection made him feel suffocated, as if he was reliving those moments of utter helplessness. Carlos had developed ways to cope, or so it seemed. He detached himself from the memories, pushing them away like a festering wound that threatened to consume him whole. When confronted with situations that even remotely reminded him of his past—such as being in an enclosed space or hearing the distant report of gunfire—he would comply with whatever was demanded of him, hoping to avoid any conflict. This tendency to fawn over those he perceived as threats had become a deeply ingrained response, a desperate attempt to prevent history from repeating itself. But there were moments when these strategies failed, and Carlos was forced to confront the abyss that lay within. When memories surfaced, they did so with the intensity of the present moment, not as distant recollections. He would see himself in that cell again, reliving the terror and the rage. His inability to articulate his experiences without becoming overwhelmed had become a source of frustration; words seemed insufficient against the tidal wave of emotions that threatened to engulf him. The aftermath of those episodes was just as debilitating. Carlos couldn't shake off the belief that he was to blame for what happened, that somehow his actions had led to his own torture. The weight of self-blame and guilt hung heavy on his shoulders, making it hard for him to forgive himself. And then there were times when rage took over, a burning fury at the injustices perpetrated against him, at the world's indifference. Carlos's fear of potential harm had become all-consuming; he believed that anyone could be a threat, that safety was merely an illusion. His trust in others had been irreparably damaged, and with it, his ability to form meaningful relationships. Even his work, once a source of pride, now felt hollow, a reminder of the fragility of life. As Carlos navigated his daily routine, these emotions simmered beneath the surface. He had become increasingly isolated, withdrawing from social interactions as he found himself unable to cope with the world around him. His widower status added another layer of loneliness to his existence, making it harder for him to find solace in human connection. It was this unbearable solitude that finally led Carlos to seek help. He realized that living in a constant state of threat and guilt had become unsustainable; he yearned for peace, for a way to confront the demons that haunted him without being consumed by them. As he sat in the therapist's office, his eyes clouded with unshed tears, Carlos knew that this was his last stand against the darkness that had pursued him for so long.
